svg.text: DELIVERABLE B: PROMPT ENGINEERING & ITERATION LOG (15 MARKS)
Structured Prompts with Labeled Schema, Grounding Constraints, Iteration Analysis, and [VERIFY] Protocol
STRUCTURED PROMPTS SPECIFICATION (PROMPTS A, B, AND C)
PROMPT A: ONE-PAGE PRINCIPAL'S BRIEF
[ROLE] Collegiate AI Productivity & Verification Lead. [AUDIENCE] College Principal & Senior Academic Council.
[CONTEXT] Ground Truth: 3-day Innovation Week; 480 registered; 312 gate entry scans; 96 voluntary feedback forms (4.1/5 avg);
Budget: ₹1,20,000 approved, ₹1,08,500 expenses; ₹75,000 confirmed sponsor transfer. No employability data collected.
[TASK] Produce a 1-page executive brief covering outcomes, financial governance, data caveats, and next steps.
[CONSTRAINTS] 1) Zero hallucinations. 2) Never claim 70% employability. 3) Do not cite NPII-7. 4) Tag uncertain points as [VERIFY].
[OUTPUT FORMAT] Executive Summary, Ground Truth Data Table, Mandatory "What We Cannot Conclude" Section, Sign-off Block.
PROMPT B: FIVE-SLIDE PRESENTATION OUTLINE (FACULTY & MANAGEMENT)
[ROLE] Academic Presentation Specialist. [AUDIENCE] Department Heads and Faculty Review Board.
[TASK] Create a structured 5-slide outline. Exactly one purpose per slide. Slide 4 must be 'What We Cannot Conclude'.
[CONSTRAINTS] Use exact numbers (312 scans, ₹1.085L spend). Emphasize that duplicate scans are unverified. Mark estimates as [VERIFY].
PROMPT C: PUBLIC SOCIAL-MEDIA POST (STUDENTS & COMMUNITY)
[ROLE] Student Communications Lead. [AUDIENCE] Student body, participants, and partner tech clubs.
[TASK] Write an energetic LinkedIn/Instagram post celebrating 3 days of student innovation and community participation.
[CONSTRAINTS] Strictly prohibited from claiming guaranteed jobs, career boosts, or employability metrics. Highlight 4.1/5 rating.
PROMPT ITERATION EXPERIMENT: BEFORE VS. AFTER COMPARISON
V1: NAIVE UNCONSTRAINED PROMPT (FAILED)
Prompt Given to AI:
"Write a one-page brief for our principal about
our Campus Innovation Week. Make it sound exciting
and mention how it helps student careers & standards."
AI Output V1 (Catastrophic Hallucinations):
• "Campus Innovation Week was a roaring success with
over 500 participants across all campus departments."
• "The event achieved a staggering 70% employability
enhancement, guaranteeing placement readiness."
• "Audited under the globally recognized NeuroPrompt
Integrity Index (NPII-7) AI quality standard."
• "100% of participants gave top marks in feedback."
Root-Cause Weaknesses Diagnosed:
1. Zero negative constraints allowed model to confabulate.
2. "Make it sound exciting" triggered promotional hallucination.
3. No Ground Truth numbers provided; model hallucinated 500.
4. No rule instructing model to admit lack of data.
V2: GROUNDED PROMPT WITH [VERIFY] PROTOCOL
Prompt Modifications Added:
• Injected full Ground Truth parameters (312 scans, 480 reg).
• Added explicit negative constraints ("Never claim 70%").
• MANDATORY RULE: If a figure is unconfirmed or duplicate
scans unchecked, you MUST tag it as [VERIFY].
AI Output V2 (Grounded & Auditable):
• "Campus Innovation Week recorded 312 gate entries out of
480 registrations [VERIFY: Deduplication pending]."
• "Financial expenditure totaled ₹1,08,500 on an approved
budget of ₹1,20,000 (90.42% utilization rate)."
• "Feedback rating averaged 4.1/5 across 96 responses."
• "What We Cannot Conclude: Employability was NOT
measured; 70% claim is unverified hearsay and rejected."
Why V2 Succeeded (Verification Rationale):
1. Negative guardrails blocked confabulation of phantom standards.
2. Mandatory [VERIFY] rule forced uncertainty into the open.
3. Output was 100% auditable against institutional receipts.
HOW WE KNOW THE PROMPT CHANGE IMPROVED THE RESULT
• Traceability Test: Every single numerical token in V2 maps directly to the case ground truth table (312, 480, 96, 4.1, ₹1.2L, ₹1.085L).
• Falsification Test: The [VERIFY] protocol successfully prevented the model from smoothing over the duplicate scan ambiguity.
• Defensibility: When submitted to the Principal, the document exposes risks rather than hiding them, safeguarding institutional integrity.
